outline.chapter_title: Introduction: The Challenge of Controlling Diffusion Models
outline.description: This chapter introduces the context of large text-to-image diffusion models, highlighting their capabilities and limitations regarding fine-grained control. It defines the core problem of adapting these models to downstream tasks without losing their pre-trained generative abilities.
subtopics: Overview of Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
Limitations of Text Guidance: Ambiguity and Lack of Precision
Defining Downstream Tasks: Subject-Driven vs. Controllable Generation
The Finetuning Dilemma: Efficiency vs. Generalizability Preservation
Critique of Existing Methods: Small Learning Rates and Additive Updates
The Need for a Structural Measure of Semantic Preservation

outline.chapter_title: Theoretical Foundations: Hyperspherical Energy and Semantics
outline.description: Before introducing the proposed method, this chapter establishes the theoretical motivation. It explains why the angular relationships between neurons (hyperspherical energy) are critical for preserving semantic information in neural networks.
subtopics: Angular Features vs. Magnitude: Evidence from Autoencoders
Defining Hyperspherical Energy (HE)
The Relationship Between Neuron Uniformity and Semantic Structure
Why Euclidean Distance is Insufficient for Measuring Model Drift
Hypothesis: Preserving HE Preserves Generative Capability

outline.description: This chapter presents the primary contribution of the paper: Orthogonal Finetuning. It details the mathematical formulation, the mechanism of applying orthogonal transformations, and why this approach theoretically guarantees the preservation of hyperspherical energy.
subtopics: The Principle of Orthogonal Transformation in Weight Spaces
Mathematical Proof: Invariance of Hyperspherical Energy under Rotation/Reflection
Formulating the Optimization Objective
Layer-Shared Orthogonal Matrices: Adjusting the Canonical Coordinate System
Initialization Strategies: Starting from Identity

outline.description: Moving from theory to practice, this chapter addresses the computational challenges of optimizing orthogonal matrices. It covers efficient parameterization techniques like Cayley transforms and block-diagonal structures to make OFT scalable.
subtopics: Challenges in Differentiable Orthogonalization
Cayley Parameterization: Generating Orthogonal Matrices from Skew-Symmetric Inputs
Block-Diagonal Structures for Reduced Complexity
Parameter Sharing Strategies Across Blocks
Comparative Analysis: OFT vs. LoRA in Terms of Parameter Count and Complexity

outline.chapter_title: Advanced Variants: Constrained and Re-scaled OFT
outline.description: This chapter explores extensions to the base OFT method designed to enhance stability and flexibility. It introduces Constrained OFT (COFT) for limiting deviation from pre-trained weights and Re-scaled OFT for learning magnitude adjustments.
subtopics: _motivation for Constraints: Balancing Flexibility and Stability_
_Constrained OFT (COFT): Imposing Radius Constraints on the Hypersphere_
_Enforcing Deviation Limits via Projected Gradient Descent on Skew-Symmetric Matrices_
_The Role of Hyperparameter Epsilon in Controlling Model Plasticity_
_Re-scaled OFT: Learning Diagonal Magnitude Coefficients Without Breaking HE_

outline.description: The final chapter summarizes the contributions of Orthogonal Finetuning,discusses its broader implications for model adaptation,and outlines open problems for future research.
subtopics: Summary of Contributions:Theory,Method,and Empirical Results
Open Problem 1:Scalability Challenges in Matrix Inversion
Open Problem 2:Compositionality-Multiplying Orthogonal Matrices for Multi-Task Learning
Open Problem 3:Improving Parameter Efficiency Beyond Block-Diagonal Bias
Final Thoughts:The Trade-off Between Flexibility and Regularity in Deep Learning
